name: GPUImage (OpenGL ES)
baseline: Core Image on iOS 5 for live camera filtering
verdict_reason: The README's 40X figure is for an iPhone 4 against iOS 5 Core Image; on an iPhone 4S the same README reports only 4X, and it says Core Image was already faster for large-radius Gaussian blurs. GPUImage is built on OpenGL ES, deprecated by Apple in iOS 12, and has had no commits since 2016, so the result says nothing about today's Metal-backed Core Image.
tier_reason: First-party numbers naming the devices, with no OS build, toolchain or raw data; the benchmark app shows results only in-app.
claimed_speedup: iPhone 4: 2.5 ms per frame vs 106 ms with Core Image (40X) and 460 ms on the CPU (184X); iPhone 4S: 4X faster than Core Image and 102X faster than CPU-bound processing.
workload: Upload a camera frame, apply a gamma filter and display it.
one_liner: OpenGL ES filter framework that beat iOS 5 Core Image by 40x on an iPhone 4 and 4x on a 4S; unmaintained since 2016.
how_it_is_fast: GPUImage uploads camera frames as OpenGL ES textures and runs each filter as a fragment shader, chaining filters through framebuffers so a frame stays on the GPU until it is displayed. In 2012 Core Image on iOS 5 carried more per-frame overhead for a simple filter like this.
use_it_when: Maintaining legacy code that already depends on it
skip_it_when: Any new code: OpenGL ES is deprecated and the project is unmaintained (its Metal successor, GPUImage3, publishes no benchmark numbers)
Large-radius blurs, where the README says Core Image was already faster
caveats: iPhone 4 and 4S against iOS 5-era Core Image; Core Image has since moved to Metal
The README's own 4S figure shrinks the gap from 40X to 4X
No build configuration or raw data published
tradeoffs: Built on OpenGL ES, which Apple deprecated in iOS 12
Lacks Core Image features such as face detection (per the README)

evidence.quote: This framework compares favorably to Core Image when handling video, taking only 2.5 ms on an iPhone 4 to upload a frame from the camera, apply a gamma filter, and display, versus 106 ms for the same operation using Core Image.
CPU-based processing takes 460 ms, making GPUImage 40X faster than Core Image for this operation on this hardware, and 184X faster than CPU-bound processing.
On an iPhone 4S, GPUImage is only 4X faster than Core Image for this case, and 102X faster than CPU-bound processing.
However, for more complex operations like Gaussian blurs at larger radii, Core Image currently outpaces GPUImage.
In comparison to Core Image (part of iOS 5.0)
